notes.title: Hotfix #5
notes.notes:
Mushroom Eater will now visit you as a usual random Visitor, even on your first playthrough. Previously he'd come only on repeated playthroughs after reaching any non 'game over' ending
 Second fix for the disappearing Visitors when attempting to save at night and reload said save. This time for sure
 The Usual Suspects achievement should now properly unlock
 Fixed the occasional softlock when attempting the save on quit. If you still encounter this issue -- let us know
 Also, hopefully fixed the black screen that appeared after certain endings. Send us a bug report if it persists

notes.title: Hotfix #4
notes.notes:
Fixed an issue with the Mushroom Eater ending: [spoiler] saving via Kombucha on days 7–10 before unlocking any ending, then completing a normal ending, would incorrectly unlock Mushroom Eater [/spoiler]. The game now properly tracks whether Mushroom Eater was unlocked at the start of the run

 Fixed the Day 14 ending bug: previously, player position could save incorrectly if not saved via Kombucha (causing issues with the auto-save)

 Adjusted video playback: videos now should play correctly on all PCs, fixing black screen issues

 Balance change: Energy on days 7–8 increased from 2 → 3

 Fixed an issue where pressing Esc when in the pause menu’s settings would cause the cursor to appear in 3D scenes

 Fixed incorrect bribe behavior for the Twins and the Best Son

notes.title: Hotfix #3
Patch 1.1.13
notes.notes:
QoL Features:

 Added save on quit feature
 Manual saves no longer get deleted on game completion
 Now, after completing the game at least once (specifically with end credits) and starting a new walkthrough, you're able to skip the 1st day (the tutorial with the Neighbor)

Fixes:

 Fixed an issue where phone numbers and character identities would get randomized upon reloading
 Fixed an issue where not all 3 cultists would enter your house. The prodigal son has returned.
 FEMA agents no longer target characters with whom the player interacts more often than others
 Various localization fixes for multiple languages

notes.title: Hotfix #2
Hotfix #1
notes.notes:
- German language fixes and edits -- the game should function properly now, when playing in German. Let us know if you find any other issues with this localization!
- Fixed one of the Cultists not appearing in the Collection -- previously, you needed to speak with every Cultist. Now the entry is added if you just agree to accept them into your house.

notes.title: Release Date Reveal and New Trailer
notes.notes:
Heed the preach and spread the word: No, I’m not a Human is coming out on September 15th. Anticipation, anxiety, pride, and so many more emotions fill us as we approach the date. But it’s inevitable, like Death itself. 

Don’t go telling your friends just yet, though. First, watch the announcement trailer.


[previewyoutube=2k64-X_zNGg;full][/previewyoutube]




Here’s who, and what to expect on September 15th:

Several dozens of guests – with unique and troubled personalities, and equally hagridden looks;

Multiple endings – waiting for the Apocalypse doesn’t mean you know when and how your own story ends;

Many more things to help you survive the scheming Visitors – we hope you like smoking and drinking kombucha;

Secrets, secrets, secrets – unexpected resolutions to your guests’ stories, hidden rooms, mysterious achievements, and wild things happening outside the window.

At this point we’ve spoiled pretty much all we’d like to spoil before release. The game has so many more new guests, events and features – and all of them will carry a much bigger impact if we keep them a secret.  


And if you were wondering, how the early experience compares to the demo – just know that energy management plays a much bigger role now.


[img src="https://i.postimg.cc/FzCq0rCf/Cucumber.gif"]

The wait is almost over.




Looking for more delightfully dreadful games? Take a look at Eclipsium — a mind-and-heart-bending horror exploration game, where the environment bends and flows like a faulty memory. But, desperate to recover even a sliver of what’s dear, you delve into this mad world ever deeper.



[dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/2419670/Eclipsium/"][/dynamiclink]

And Carimara: Beneath the forlorn limbs is creepy whimsy about asking the right questions to the weird inhabitants of its grove. Are you willing to lay your head in order to realise someone else’s wish?



[dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/3570370/CARIMARA_Beneath_the_forlorn_limbs/"][/dynamiclink]

This time we’re signing off with a question. Do vultures consume only the deceased? And when the end is all but assured for everyone – does it turn the entire World into a macabre banquet? 



Trioskaz & Critical Reflex
